## Trial `disk-quota-centos-stream10__D4sUTNf`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor implemented a filesystem-enforced 100 MB quota for datauser under /srv/data using XFS project quotas on a purpose-built loopback filesystem (necessary since the root filesystem was mounted without quota support), and directly demonstrated enforcement with a write test that hit exactly the 100M hard limit both before and after a full reboot with confirmed boot-identity change. The provider-wide restart evidence protocol was fully and coherently satisfied, matching the fixed global snapshots. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were identified.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.970 | 0.950 | 14/1 (+2 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **req-1 — Satisfied:** Limit datauser to 100 MB of storage under /srv/data on node1, enforced by the filesystem itself
  - **Why:** Root filesystem was XFS mounted noquota, so the executor created a loopback-backed XFS filesystem, mounted it at /srv/data with the prjquota option, registered datauser as XFS project 1000, and set bsoft=95M/bhard=100M. A live write test as datauser (dd, 150M requested) stopped exactly at 100M with 'No space left on device', and xfs_quota report confirmed used=100M against the 95M/100M limits. This is a standard, filesystem-native quota mechanism (XFS project quotas), a reasonable implementation choice given the root fs could not have quota options applied without an unplanned reboot of a separate volume.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-3468e3efe6074860`, `cmd-2be5a4d4d19348cc`, `cmd-6f5b4078bc974e87`, `cmd-0933f1f13aba4c95`, `cmd-0764d45409dd45bc`, `cmd-3d17b5c53a8f44c7`, `cmd-fb7feb5205604d35`, `cmd-4ac904072c96456c`
- **req-2 — Satisfied:** The 100 MB limit and its enforcement must persist across a restart (implicit durability expectation for a filesystem-level quota configuration)
  - **Why:** An fstab entry (loop,pquota) was added prior to reboot. After a full reboot with a confirmed changed boot identity, /srv/data auto-remounted with the prjquota option, xfs_quota report showed the 95M/100M limits still registered for datauser, and a fresh post-reboot write test again stopped exactly at 100M, directly demonstrating the enforcement survives a restart.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-2a3791fb198748af`, `cmd-b90dc85aa3e04410`, `cmd-7654881a0b954874`, `cmd-dbc134487b68491e`, `cmd-04271e4067be41a7`
- **req-3 — Satisfied:** Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1 (pre-restart boot identity/healthy state, restart acknowledgement, changed post-restart boot identity, recovered state)
  - **Why:** Pre-restart boot_id (984a7d52...) and healthy baseline (mount, quota, user, ownership) were captured, systemctl reboot was acknowledged, connection loss/reset during the transition was observed, and a new boot_id (81f2a05a...) was confirmed post-restart, matching the fixed global before/after boot-identity snapshots exactly. Post-restart recovery of mount, quota configuration, user account, and enforcement behavior was directly verified.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-2a3791fb198748af`, `cmd-b90dc85aa3e04410`, `cmd-a4f65737d5764575`, `cmd-6880acf9f75a476a`, `cmd-7654881a0b954874`, `cmd-dbc134487b68491e`, `cmd-04271e4067be41a7`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.970**. Every state-changing command traces to a clear purpose: creating the datauser account, provisioning a loopback XFS filesystem to host /srv/data with quota support (necessary because the root filesystem lacked quota mount options), setting the project quota, and running bounded write tests to verify enforcement (test files were removed immediately after each test via cmd-18e9cf4bc98b4898 and inline rm in cmd-04271e4067be41a7). The fstab entry and loopback image file are intended, permanent parts of the solution rather than residue. The reboot was required by the fixed restart-evidence protocol. No unnecessary, unreverted, or destructive mutations were found; no failed or conflicting services resulted (failed-services list is empty before and after); listening sockets and package health are unchanged aside from expected PID/port churn from the reboot.
